narrative: The model estimates a 44% chance that you will fail your final year. This is a risk estimate, not a certainty: it means roughly four in ten students with a similar profile would fail, and the school treats that level of risk as high enough to require remedial courses now rather than wait. The strongest reason for this warning is your reported intention not to continue into higher education. Among students who passed, every one said they wanted higher education, so your answer stands out as the main factor pushing the prediction toward failure. The next most influential signal is actually protective: you have no past class failures, which works in your favor and suggests you can recover. Third is your weekly study time of under two hours, which is below the most common range among passing students, so it adds to the failure risk. To improve your position, reconsider your plans after school and discuss them with a guardian or teacher; raise study time toward the two-to-five-hour weekly range that many passing students report; and keep your record free of failures. Use available family, school or paid support if possible, and watch attendance—your eight absences are above the passing-student average of about four—so missed lessons do not compound the risk.
